messages:
alex: Quick flag 1:10 UTC. Noticed two Xid and ECC single-bit alerts in rack-7 of gpu-pool-us-east-1. Nodes gpu-07 and gpu-09. No user-facing errors yet.

sangeeta: Can you paste the exact kernel + nvidia lines? keep it short, we dont need full dmesg for every event.

alex: pasted snippet below (most recent first):
```
[2024-04-02T21:10:03Z] NVRM: Xid (Fault): 31, GPU=0000:65:00.0, Reason: 0x00000086
[2024-04-02T21:10:03Z] nvidia: GPU 0000:65:00.0: ECC single-bit error detected
[2024-04-02T21:10:04Z] nvidia: SM exception on GPU 0
[2024-04-02T21:10:05Z] kernel: pcieport 0000:61:00.0: AER: Corrected error received: id=00e0
```

mike: I also ran `nvidia-smi -q -x` at 21:10:10. Driver 535.x. ECC flagged ON, but sample collector did not show persistent ECC counter increments.

julia: Did any heavy jobs start around that time? high sequence-length or big batch?

alex: Runner logs show a transformer job with batch=128 started 21:07 UTC on gpu-07. No network blips.

kai: Idea: envelope approach. Send a compact, gzipped "gpu-event envelope" whenever an OOM/Xid/ECC/thermal event is detected. Not full dmesg. Envelope = metadata header + small kernel window + NVML snapshot + container->PID map.

sangeeta: Agreed. Full dumps for every event are too noisy and expensive. Need clear heuristics for when to escalate full dump: e.g., same GPU 3 events in 24h, or any double-bit ECC.

alex: Proposed envelope fields (minimal):
- node (hostname), region, rack
- gpu_uuid, pci_addr, gpu_index
- event_ts, xid_code, ecc_kind (single|double|none), driver_version
- kernel_window_before (n lines), kernel_window_after (n lines)
- nvml_snapshot (temp, mem_total, mem_used, util, ecc_count)
- process_list (top 10 by gpu mem: pid, cmd, gpu_mem)
- monotonic_offset & host_uptime to align sources

mike: Also include kernel sequence number (dmesg line number) and current `sysctl kernel.printk` so we can detect dropped messages. For parsing we should canonicalize Xid reasons to root-cause buckets: ECC, thermal, PCIe, driver, context.

julia: From collection side: run these commands with a small wrapper to avoid scanning entire journal on boot: `journalctl -k --since "@${EVENT_TS}-5m" --output=short-iso`. And include `dmesg --ctime | sed -n "${START},${END}p"`. Gzip the envelope.

kai: My prototype extraction (sketch):
```
EVENT_TS=$(date -u -Iseconds)
XID_LINE=$(dmesg | tac | grep -m1 -E "Xid \(|NVRM:")
LINE_NUM=$(dmesg -T | nl -ba | grep -F "$XID_LINE" | awk '{print $1}')
START=$((LINE_NUM-15))
END=$((LINE_NUM+15))
dmesg -T | sed -n "${START},${END}p" | gzip -9 > /tmp/envelope-${EVENT_TS}.dmesg.gz
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=timestamp,index,uuid,name,driver_version,temperature.gpu,utilization.gpu,memory.total,memory.used,unit_ecc.errors --format=csv -f /tmp/envelope-${EVENT_TS}.nvml.csv
```

sangeeta: Permission model: collectors should run as non-root where possible. Use `nvidia-smi` and NVML via `nvidia-container-toolkit` bindings; otherwise run a small privileged agent with strict RBAC.

alex: Cost math quick check: gzipped envelope ~6-12KB. At 15k events/mo -> ~180MB/mo. Full dmesg dumps ~1.5MB each -> 22.5GB/mo. Envelope is clearly cheaper.

mike: For the parser: normalize Xid codes into a mapping table that points to likely mitigations (e.g., drain+replace for repeated ECC double-bit, schedule kernel/driversupgrade for known driver bug IDs, NVLink: check topo and link resets). Keep a rolling 7-day recurrence counter keyed by GPU UUID.

julia: Also make sure to cryptographically sign envelopes for private clusters and S3 upload with per-customer KMS.

kai: Edge case note: some SKUs don't increment single-bit counters reliably under driver 535.x. Parser should consult a driver-bugmap and mark counters as questionable.

alex: Proposed operational flow: 1) local detector sees Xid/ECC/thermal 2) build envelope, upload to central bucket and post short event to Datadog with envelope pointer 3) parsing service mines envelope, increments recurrence, and if thresholds hit (3 events/24h or any double-bit) trigger drain/replace + request full dump.

sangeeta: OK. Next steps: kai to open PR for prototype agent, mike/julia to implement small parser + mapping table, ops to create an alert for recurrence and escalation. I'll run a cost runbook and permission checklist for tomorrow's sync.

infra-bot: deploy queued: infra/gpu-event-agent/proto -> staging at 2024-04-03T02:45:00Z :rocket:

mike: one more: add monotonic timestamps to each snippet so we can order events even with clock skew.

alex: I'll draft an RFC with the envelope schema and example artifacts, will tag @oncall and security. Keep replies brief here and move design to PR.

julia: :thumbsup:
